alg-benjamini-yekutieli-step-up-procedur:
## Definition

Input an integer $m\ge1$, observed values $p_1,\ldots,p_m\in[0,1]$ of p-value statistics ([[def-p-value]]), and a target level $q\in(0,1)$. Let $H_m=\sum_{j=1}^m1/j$ be the harmonic number from [[def-harmonic-number-for-set-cover-analysis]]. For $k=1,\ldots,m$, set

$$c_k:=\frac{kq}{mH_m}.$$

Order the pairs $(p_i,i)$ lexicographically, so equal values are ordered by their original indices, and write the ordered values $p_{(1)}\le\cdots\le p_{(m)}$. Set

$$R:=\max\bigl(\{k\in\{1,\ldots,m\}:p_{(k)}\le c_k\}\cup\{0\}\bigr).$$

Reject exactly the hypotheses at ranks $1,\ldots,R$; when $R=0$, reject none. Because $H_m\ge1$, each critical value satisfies $0<c_k\le q/H_m\le q<1$. This definition specifies the procedure; no FDR guarantee is asserted here.
lem-unit-interval-is-standard-borel:
## Statement

Let $I=[0,1]$ with the subspace topology from the usual real topology and with its Borel sigma-algebra. Then $(I,\mathcal B(I))$ is a standard-Borel space ([[def-standard-borel-space]]).
lem-step-up-leave-one-out-rejection-part:
## Statement

Let $m\ge1$, $p=(p_1,\ldots,p_m)\in[0,1]^m$, and critical values $0<c_1\le\cdots\le c_m\le1$. Define the step-up rule by

$$R:=\max\bigl(\{k\in\{1,\ldots,m\}:p_{(k)}\le c_k\}\cup\{0\}\bigr),$$

rejecting exactly ranks $1,\ldots,R$. Fix $i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}$. Write the remaining values in increasing order as $y_{(1)}\le\cdots\le y_{(m-1)}$, and set $y_{(0)}=0$. For $1\le k\le m$, let

$$C_{i,k}:=\{y_{(k-1)}\le c_k\}\cap\bigcap_{r=k}^{m-1}\{y_{(r)}>c_{r+1}\},$$

with an empty intersection interpreted as the whole remaining-coordinate space. Put $D_{i,k}:=\bigcup_{j=1}^k C_{i,j}$. Then:

1. Whenever $p_i\le c_k$, the rule has exactly $R=k$ rejections and rejects $i$ if and only if $p_{-i}\in C_{i,k}$.
2. The sets $C_{i,1},\ldots,C_{i,m}$ are a disjoint Borel partition of $[0,1]^{m-1}$.
3. For $k<m$,
   $$D_{i,k}=\bigcap_{r=k}^{m-1}\{y_{(r)}>c_{r+1}\},$$
   and $D_{i,m}$ is the whole space. Each $D_{i,k}$ is a coordinatewise increasing Borel set.

For $m=1$, the remaining-coordinate space is the singleton empty tuple, and $C_{i,1}=D_{i,1}$ is the whole space.
def-prds-on-true-null-coordinates:
## Definition

Let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$ be a probability space, let $m\ge1$, and let $\mathbf P=(P_1,\ldots,P_m):\Omega\to[0,1]^m$ be a random vector whose coordinates are p-value statistics ([[def-p-value]]). Fix a designated true-null index set $I_0\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}$. For $i\in I_0$, write $\mu_i$ for the law of $P_i$ under $\mathbb P$ and define its support relative to $[0,1]$ by

$$\operatorname{supp}(\mu_i):=\{x\in[0,1]:\mu_i(U)>0\text{ for every relatively open neighborhood }U\text{ of }x\}.$$

Give each coordinate $[0,1]$ its trace Borel sigma-algebra ([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]) and give $[0,1]^m$ the finite product sigma-algebra ([[def-product-sigma-algebra-and-finite-product-sigma-algebras]]). In this definition, “Borel set” means a member of that product sigma-algebra; thus “increasing measurable set” means coordinatewise increasing in this stated structure. The unit-interval lemma proves that $[0,1]$ with this trace Borel structure is standard Borel ([[lem-unit-interval-is-standard-borel]]). The finite-product result then makes $[0,1]^m$ with the specified product sigma-algebra a standard-Borel target ([[def-standard-borel-space]], [[lem-finite-products-of-standard-borel-spaces-are-standard-borel]]); its finite-product proof uses only finite choice in ZF. Under the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), this target has a regular conditional distribution given $\sigma(P_i)$, and the conditional-law factorization result supplies a kernel $K_i:[0,1]\to[0,1]^m$ representing the conditional law of $\mathbf P$ given $P_i=x$ ([[thm-existence-of-regular-conditional-distributions-for-standard-borel-targets]], [[lem-regular-conditional-kernels-factor-through-a-standard-borel-conditioning-variable]], [[def-conditional-law-given-a-random-element]]).

The law of $\mathbf P$ is **positive regression dependent on the true-null coordinates (PRDS on $I_0$)** if, for each $i\in I_0$, such a conditional-law version can be chosen so that for every coordinatewise increasing Borel set $D$, the function

$$x\longmapsto K_i(x,D)$$

is nondecreasing on $\operatorname{supp}(\mu_i)$. If $I_0=\varnothing$, this condition is vacuous. The monotonicity condition is a full conditional-law requirement; pairwise correlations alone do not verify it.
thm-by-fdr-control-under-arbitrary-depen:
## Statement

Let $\mathsf E=((\mathcal X,\mathcal A),\Theta,(P_\theta)_{\theta\in\Theta})$ be a statistical experiment ([[def-statistical-experiment]]), let $m\ge1$, and fix a finite family of null hypotheses $H_{01},\ldots,H_{0m}$. For each $i$, let $p_i$ be a p-value statistic valid for $H_{0i}$ in the sense of [[def-null-valid-p-value-and-fwer-fdr]]. For $\theta\in\Theta$, put

$$I_0(\theta):=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}:\theta\in H_{0i}\},\qquad m_0(\theta):=|I_0(\theta)|.$$

For every $q\in(0,1)$, the BY procedure in [[alg-benjamini-yekutieli-step-up-procedure]] satisfies

$$\operatorname{FDR}_\theta\le\frac{m_0(\theta)}{m}q\le q.$$

No dependence condition on the joint law of the p-values is required.
lem-bh-prds-null-contribution-bound:
## Statement

Let $P=(P_1,\ldots,P_m)$ be p-value random variables in a probability space, let $m\ge1$, $q\in(0,1)$, and fix an index $i$ in a designated true-null set $I_0$. Suppose $P_i$ is valid under this law and the law of $P$ is PRDS on $I_0$ as defined in [[def-prds-on-true-null-coordinates]]. Apply BH at level $q$, and let $I_i$ indicate that $i$ is rejected and $R$ be the total number rejected. Then

$$\mathbb E\!\left[\frac{I_i}{R\vee1}\right]\le\frac qm.$$
thm-bh-fdr-control-under-prds:
## Statement

Let $\mathsf E=((\mathcal X,\mathcal A),\Theta,(P_\theta)_{\theta\in\Theta})$ be a statistical experiment, let $m\ge1$, and fix a finite family of null hypotheses $H_{01},\ldots,H_{0m}$ with p-value statistics $p_1,\ldots,p_m$ valid for their respective nulls. For each $\theta$, write

$$I_0(\theta):=\{i:\theta\in H_{0i}\},\qquad m_0(\theta):=|I_0(\theta)|.$$

Assume the Axiom of Choice as required for the regular conditional-law interface in [[def-prds-on-true-null-coordinates]]. Suppose that, under every $P_\theta$, the p-value vector $(p_1(X),\ldots,p_m(X))$ is PRDS on $I_0(\theta)$. Then for every $q\in(0,1)$, the ordinary BH procedure in [[alg-benjamini-hochberg-step-up-procedure]] satisfies

$$\operatorname{FDR}_\theta\le\frac{m_0(\theta)}m q\le q.$$

The PRDS assumption is imposed only on the true-null coordinates; no independence assumption is made.
